evidence.positive: Created a demo-demo case for a diabetic patient with no recent glucose (patient or2840b-fake-e6b8810c..., caseId 37543, operation staged with a null start time so case start would run), then drove a real case start with POST /api/admin/events/category-event {eventCategories:[START_MONITORING]}. The app logged 'Processing a case start' / 'Simulating case start' and a-preop-glucose fired through the silent app-launch path: rule_fired_results row 01a03ff9-... with rule_identifier=a-preop-glucose, rule_execution_contexts.evaluation_mode=SILENT, accepted=null, details EVALUATION_DATE=1787779392945 (2026-08-26T21:23:12.945Z), and its fire-time compliance_results row was compliant=f. Posted a GLUCOSE observation with effective_time 2026-08-26T21:26:00Z (2m47s after the firing) via POST /api/admin/observations/patient/{pmrn}/case/37543, then drove CLOSE_APP at 21:26:54. Log showed 'Evaluating compliance for case stop: operation=CaseId[value=37543]' followed by 'Found 1 rule firings to evaluate at case stop for operation: CaseId[value=37543]'. compliance_results.compliant flipped f -> t, and GET /api/admin/rule/evaluations/fired?caseId=37543&ruleIdentifier=a-preop-glucose returned [{"rule":"a-preop-glucose","accepted":null,"compliance":[{"label":"alert-compliance","compliant":true}]}].
evidence.negative: Two inverse cases run against the same silent firing (window anchored at 21:23:12.945Z). (a) Glucose before the window: soft-deleted the in-window observation and posted one at 21:20:00Z, 3m13s BEFORE the firing, then re-sent CLOSE_APP (end_time 21:29:56.604). compliance_results.compliant = f, live glucose list '2026-08-26 21:20:00'. (b) Glucose past the buffer: posted one at 21:33:30Z, 10m17s after the firing, and sent CLOSE_APP at 21:34:24 so the case end was later than firing+10min and the window was the full ten minutes ending 21:33:12.945Z. compliance_results.compliant = f. A glucose that exists for the patient but falls outside [firing, firing+10min] therefore does not clear the firing, and the admin API for case 39407 (see red_check) likewise still reads compliant=false.
evidence.red_check: Two independent flips, both reverted. (1) Data flip across the boundary: with everything else identical on case 37543, glucose at 21:33:30Z (10m17s after the firing) gave compliant=f; deleting it and posting the same value at 21:33:00Z (9m47s after the firing) and re-sending CLOSE_APP gave compliant=t. A 30-second move across the ten-minute edge is what changes the verdict; the case was left in the in-window (compliant) state. (2) Pre-fix code swap: moved /app/classes/com/guided/orci/engine/rule/compliance/GlucoseCheckComplianceEvaluator.class out of the running container (md5 3f58522a54c2b7bef63f4bb0082f5103, copied to scratch first) and restarted it. That reproduces the pre-fix state exactly, because AlertComplianceEvaluator reclaims any alert firing no AlertComplianceOverride bean claims, and the app booted clean in 11.7s. Re-sending CLOSE_APP on case 37543, with the in-window 21:26:00Z glucose still in place, drove compliant from t back to f. A second case created, fired and stopped entirely inside that pre-fix window (caseId 39407, silent a-preop-glucose firing at 21:28:33.807Z, glucose at 21:28:45Z i.e. 12s later, stopped 21:28:49) also came out compliant=f, logging 'Evaluating compliance for case stop: operation=CaseId[value=39407]'. Restored the class (md5sum in the container re-verified as 3f58522a54c2b7bef63f4bb0082f5103), restarted, confirmed the file is present, and re-sent CLOSE_APP on 37543: compliant returned to t. Container /tmp holds no leftover backup and the git worktree is clean.

red_check_signature: Evaluating compliance for case stop: operation=CaseId[value=39407]
caveats: The pre-fix state throws no exception and logs no distinct message - the red result is a compliance_results row, not a stack trace - so the signature above is the case-stop line for case 39407, which was created, fired and stopped only while the pre-fix build was live and appears exactly once in the whole container log.

Only a-preop-glucose was driven end to end; a-insulin-glucose-check and a-no-insulin-glucose-check share the same evaluator and were confirmed at runtime to carry COMPLIANCE_GLUCOSE_CHECK in rule_definitions, but their firings were not reproduced (a-no-insulin-glucose-check is flag-gated to Mayo tenants and unreachable in demo-demo).

The corrected verdict only lands at case stop: at fire time the window has not elapsed, so the row is written non-compliant and CLOSE_APP is the only pass that revisits it (ComplianceResultRunner defaults to missing-only and skips rows that already exist). A case that never emits CLOSE_APP keeps the non-compliant fire-time verdict - this is what the commit message states as intended, and case 39407 still reads compliant=false after the restore for exactly that reason.

The refactor that moved silent/interactive alert logic into RuleComplianceEvaluator.defaultAlertCompliance was not exercised at runtime for non-glucose alerts; that regression surface rests on the existing unit tests.
Validation ran in the demo-demo tenant with observations injected through the admin debugger endpoint rather than an HL7 or FHIR feed.

automation.assessment: Coverage shipped with the change is already thorough and should not be duplicated: GlucoseCheckComplianceEvaluatorTest pins the mode matrix, the EVALUATION_DATE anchor in its Instant / epoch-millis / absent forms, the operation-end clamp and a firing at or after case end; ObservationRepositoryGlucoseWindowTest pins both inclusive bounds, plus or minus one millisecond, soft-deleted rows, other patients and other observation types against a real Postgres; RuleComplianceServiceGuardTest asserts the new category is in the case-stop list; AlertComplianceEvaluatorTest asserts the override defers correctly. The one path nothing covers is the one this validation exercised by hand: a real silent firing plus a CLOSE_APP event producing the corrected verdict, i.e. the EventService to RuleComplianceService wiring that every unit test stubs out. Minor placement nit worth folding in - ObservationRepositoryGlucoseWindowTest sits in orci/src/test while the other repository @DataJpaTest classes live in orci-repositories.
proposed_tests: Integration test: a CLOSE_APP category event on a case carrying a SILENT glucose-alert firing plus a glucose inside the ten-minute buffer flips the fire-time non-compliant row to compliant, covering the EventService afterCommit to evaluateComplianceForCaseOnStop wiring.
Same integration test's inverse: a glucose one minute past the buffer leaves the row non-compliant, and a glucose before the firing leaves it non-compliant.

Integration test: a firing that gets no CLOSE_APP event keeps its non-compliant fire-time verdict, locking in the documented limitation so a future change to ComplianceResultRunner's missing-only default is noticed.

qa-suite supplemental clinical-rules spec: stage a diabetic demo case, drive START_MONITORING, post a glucose inside versus outside the buffer, drive CLOSE_APP, and assert the compliance entry from GET /api/admin/rule/evaluations/fired.
Move ObservationRepositoryGlucoseWindowTest to orci-repositories so it sits with the other repository tests.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: A silent a-preop-glucose firing on a demo case was credited as compliant once a glucose was documented 2m47s later and the case was stopped.
Negative: The same firing stayed non-compliant when the only glucose sat 3m13s before it, and again when it sat 10m17s after it.
Red check: Moving that glucose 30 seconds across the ten-minute edge flipped the verdict, and removing the new evaluator class from the running container reproduced the old non-compliant result before the class was restored.

Automation: Unit and repository coverage already pins the window bounds, so the gap worth adding is an integration test for the case-stop event wiring.
